Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – FEBRUARY 3, 2022

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on February 3, 2022,
via Zoom. Commissioner McLemore called the meeting to order at 6:05 p.m. followed by the flag
salute.

Roll Call

Present
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District 2
  Commissioner Cynthia, McLemore, District 3
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation, and Community Services
  Bharat Devlia, Food Services Manager
  Gilbert Gonzalez, Graffiti Abatement Supervisor
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District 1
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District 4

Public Comments
  None

Approval of the Minutes

  Commissioner Fragoso made the motion to approve the minutes from November 4, 2021.
Commissioner McLemore seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, and Brown
  Nays: None

Director’s Business

  Stephanie Maldonado introduced a staff report recommending the Park and Recreation
Commission receive and file a staff report regarding payment of invoices in the amount of $8,000 to
Hannibal Media Group for services rendered during planning for the City’s 39th Annual King Day
Celebration.

  Commissioner Fragoso made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner Brown
seconded. The staff report was approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore, and Brown
  Nays: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – FEBRUARY 3, 2022

Verbal Reports

  Gilbert Gonzalez gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the
following:
   Parks Maintenance Division was busy working on a few projects consisting of:
  1. Replanting 35 flats of ground flowers
  2. Replacing mulch along the center medians at Century Boulevard
  3. Planting six (6) trees and 18 yards of playground wood fiber at Queen Park
   The Graffiti Abatement staff has also been busy in Districts 3 and 4 due to heavily being
  tagged on store fronts, buildings, and alleyways in the areas of Arbor Vitae and Inglewood
  Avenue to La Brea and Century Boulevard, Prairie Avenue from Imperial Highway to Century
  Boulevard. Vincent Park located in District 1 has experienced an increase in tagging. Staff
  is concentrating on working in all key entry points into the city, ensuring these areas are free
  from graffiti.

  Teresa Estrada gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   Zumba: as a result of the current surge of the COVID-19 Omicron Variant, we are taking
  additional steps to keep our patrons and community members safe. As of Tuesday, January
  4th, all indoor Zumba classes held on Tuesday evenings at Rogers Park have been canceled.
  Classes will resume on March 15th. The Saturday Zumba classes will continue, however,
  they will be moved to the outdoor patio area at Rogers Park. Zumba with Ronnie is held on
  Saturdays from 9:30 a.m. -10:30 a.m. The cost is $4 per class. You can register at
  www.parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.
   Youth Basketball: We are excited to announce that our Inglewood Youth Basketball League
  will begin on Saturday, February 12th. While canceling the 2022 season would have been
  the easy route to take, the Parks, Recreation, and Community Services Department knows
  the impact COVID-19 has had on our youth. We are committed to balancing the needs of
  our community while maintaining an environment that is safe for our employees and the
  children, adults, and families we serve. The Los Angeles County Department of Public
  Health has created Protocols for Organized Youth Sports to allow children to participate in
  organized sports and activities safely. To support and enhance the safety for all and to lower
  the risk of COVID-19 transmission, weekly testing is required for all participants. Players,
  coaches, staff, volunteers, referees, officials, and spectators are also required to wear
  masks regardless of vaccination status. We are excited to serve over 165 boys and girls
  ages 4-14. Games will be played on Saturdays at both Rogers and Darby Parks.

  Abel Canel, Recreation Supervisor (oversees the Eastside Recreation Facilities, Darby and
Center Parks, and the Lockhaven Community Center) gave a verbal report on behalf of the
Recreation Division regarding the following:

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – FEBRUARY 3, 2022

    Health Education: join us on Saturday, February 12th for a one-hour VIRTUAL class that will
  focus on “Understanding & Managing Hypertension and other Cardiac Diseases". The class
  will provide education, insight, and resources that will assist in improving your health today
  and empower you to continue to make healthier decisions tomorrow. Due to the surge in
  COVID-19, we have moved the in-person class to ZOOM. The class is free and we
  encourage everyone to attend.  You can register for the class at
  parksrec.cityofinglewood.org.

  Mr. Canel introduced himself to the Commission and gave a background about himself,
previous job experience, and education.

  Bharat Devlia gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Transportation: Our Senior and Disabled Transportation Program continues to provide trips
  to critical appointments such as dialysis and doctors' appointments. Drivers, as well as
  passengers, continue to wear face masks mandated by the Federal Transit Authority (FTA)
  as well as practice safe social distancing during transport. We have also been scheduling
  our drivers to transport our seniors and persons with disabilities to other next-day requested
  appointments.
   Nutrition: Enrollments in our Elderly Nutrition Program have stabilized over the last few
  months, with an average of 300 seniors receiving seven (7) meals per week. We continue
  to deliver weekly fresh produce in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning Institute,
  and monthly shelf-stable meal packages in collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank.
  Our annual menu planning is upon us, we welcome any suggestions and ideas on what you
  would like to enjoy on the next menu cycle, which will start on July 1, 2022.
   Senior Classes and Activities: The Inglewood Senior Center has temporarily shut down its
  limited classes and activities due to the recent Omicron variant surge. We want to ensure
  that our seniors are as safe as possible during this time.
   CACFP Meals Program: Our Child and Adult Care Food Program, or CACFP, is actively
  operating at Darby Park and Rogers Parks, serving 292 meals in the last week of January,
  and 240 meals in the week before that.
  Sabrina Barnes gave a verbal report regarding:
    NFL at the Parks Activities: The city partnered with NFL Green Initiative. Their goal is to
  provide greener environments through a variety of activities ranging from planting trees to
  resolving water matters. First, we planted 56 trees at Vincent Park, painted and planted
  flowers with the help of close to 100 volunteers. Partnering again with NFL, we completed a
  garden refresh at Queen Park. With the help of roughly 70 volunteers, we replanted the
  garden beds with flowers, six (6) trees were planted, the playground was freshened up with
  new wood chips and mulch, and lots of painting was done. All funded by mini-grants provided
  by the NFL.

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – FEBRUARY 3, 2022

    Currently in progress at Darby Park is the refreshing of the outdoor basketball courts with
  the help of a partnership between Nike and Shoe Palace. On February 12, 2022, they will
  unveil the new courts with a small clinic and presentation to the kids.
    Similarly, HBO will complete a project at Rogers Park refreshing the basketball courts by
  working with an artist to add artwork.
    Dwight Howard of the Los Angeles Lakers and the National Basketball Association (NBA)
  held a special clinic at Edward Vincent, Jr. Park.
    Capital Improvement Projects Update:
   Edward Vincent Park Restroom improvement project scheduled to begin after the
  Super Bowl activities. Wednesday, February 9, 2022, is the NFL Play 60 event with
  around 700 participants. Construction will begin when the event is over with an
  anticipated completion date being in the second week of August.
   Currently in development is a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the Vincent Park
  irrigation system improvement project which will improve the irrigation infrastructure
  as well as the landscaping. Expecting proposals to be submitted within the next two
  (2) weeks.
   Darby Park's Restroom Improvement Project is set to get underway in the coming
  months. We anticipate project approval by the City Council by April 5, 2022, with a
  tentative construction date of May 22, 2022 and completion by December 22, 2022.
  Construction will start with the restroom closest to the main building relocating the
  restroom to the current pool area. Remain a portion of the restroom will be used for
  storage or as a concession stand.
   Vincent Park pump track is scheduled for construction by the end of February with
  a 10-week completion status.
   The maintenance area will also be replaced at Vincent Park, RFP process is
  currently underway.
   Discussions have been held regarding the picnic structure area and ball diamonds
  with Dodgers RBI and Major League Baseball to complete a project. Additional
  information to come in the next few weeks.

  Commissioner Brown stated the Golden Shovel event was excellent and commended staff
on a great job with the Turkey Giveaway at SoFi Stadium. Sabrina Barnes thanked Commissioner
Brown for supporting and volunteering at all three (3) events.

  Commissioner McLemore asked if the Senior Center was open. Bharat Devlia stated it is
currently not open. Commissioner McLemore asked when it will be opened. Mr. Devlia stated they're
watching the Omicron numbers and although they want to open it's best to stay closed until it's safe.
Sabrina Barnes informed the Commission that the Senior Center was opened with limited access
due to the numbers. Los Angeles County enacted restrictions including meals and activities on or
around January 6 or 7, 2022 due to the surge. City Hall was also restricted to appointment only.
Recreation Center classes and activities except for the Early Learners Program were also
suspended.

  4
   Park and Recreation Commission

  MINUTES – FEBRUARY 3, 2022

Public Comments

  Imhotep Coleman introduced himself and gave an introduction to Urban Academy, a film
academy for high school students located on Van Ness Avenue and Manchester Boulevard. They
meet on Saturdays and are working on shooting a small film on March 5, 2022, at Darby Park. He
looks forward to working with staff.

Commissioner’s Comments

  Commissioner Brown was sorry that the city’s Annual Dr. King Day Parade and Festival was
cancelled.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:35 p.m.
